Senior Full Stack Software Engineer: Telehealth + Ecommerce (Startup, High Ownership, AI-Forward)

**About the Role:**

Enhance.MD is a telehealth company operating two consumer platforms: one providing GLP-1 weight management and longevity care, the other focused on women's health and biomarker-driven care. We’re a fast-paced startup building a team of passionate, self-starting, talented individuals who want to contribute to the telehealth + ecommerce space.

We're bringing this role in-house to take direct, hands-on ownership of that codebase from our outside development team. You'll be the person who actually knows how the system works: everything from product SKUs, intakes, orders, subscriptions, dashboards, and the AI features layered on top of them. You will continue to build and ship new ecommerce and AI-powered features while maintaining what is already live for real patients.

This is an individual contributor role. You won't be managing a team, but you will be trusted with real architectural judgment: knowing when to refactor and when to take a new approach – your ideas are welcome and will be relied on for decision making.

**What You’ll Work On:**

1. Building New Features

* Work alongside Product and Marketing teams to scope and prioritize high impact features
* Design and implement a clean, scalable patient-facing featuring
* Work within the core systems across ecommerce + telehealth workflows
* Deliver strong foundations (APIs, data models, services) where they are missing
* Integrate AI-powered features into real product workflows

2. Stabilizing & Improving the Existing Platform

* Work across a live system with real users and real complexity
* Debug issues across services, data flows, and integrations
* Partner with customer support and operations to resolve dev-related issues quickly
* Identify root causes behind recurring issues and reduce requests through systemic fixes

3. Creating Engineering Structure

* Define and implement:
* Development workflows
* Code quality standards
* Definition of Done
* Automated testing practices
* **Bring consistency across frontend, backend, and APIs**
* Improve how the team delivers, not just what it builds

**What We’re Looking For:**

Leadership & Ownership

* You take responsibility for outcomes
* You can set direction without overcomplicating things
* You introduce structure that increases speed

Execution & Business Thinking

* You can translate business priorities into shipped features
* You are able to effectively communicate with non-technical business partners
* You understand that shipping matters more than perfection Strong analytical mindset: you break down problems, identify root causes, and make data-informed decisions
* Business-aware: you understand tradeoffs between speed, cost, and impact, and prioritize accordingly
* You think beyond single tasks: you understand how your work affects the business, operations, and customer experience

Technical Judgment

* Strong system design and architectural thinking
* Comfortable working in evolving, imperfect environments
* Able to push back on requirements when needed, clearly communicating tradeoffs and impact
* Forward-thinking as you anticipate downstream effects and avoid decisions that create unnecessary complexity or risk
* Comfortable calling out when a solution is too costly, too fragile, or negatively impacts other parts of the system, and proposing better alternatives

AI & Development Style

We move fast and use AI to do it. We are looking for someone who can:

* Be comfortable using a variety of AI tools, open to adopting new ones
* Know when to prototype quickly versus apply engineering rigor
* Be excited about using AI to improve both development speed and product capabilities

**Technical Skills**

Core Stack

* Microservices Architecture - FastAPI (Python) and ASP.NET Core (C#)
* UI - React/NextJS, TypeScript
* Backend Databases: Redis, PostgreSQL
* Cloud Environment: GCP, Container Apps, IaaC (TF), GitHub Actions
* AI Development: Azure Foundry with Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Agent Framework
* AI Native Development Practices: Includes Skill development, AI Agent Development, Obsidian AI Brain

Software Engineering Skills

* You understand of Microservices architecture and multi-tenant platform design
* You understand pub-sub and eventual consistency models
* You understand DDD (Domain-Driven Design) and Software Architecture principles such as ACL (Anti-Corruption Layer), Events-Driven design, Ports & Adapter design
* You understand AI-native development and can develop AI agents and skills to assist in daily workflows
* You understand the 12 Factor Framework for Software Development
* Nice to have: experience working with Saleor

Security & Compliance

* Experience or strong awareness of: HIPAA / healthcare data handling
* Data privacy and security best practices
* **Understands how to: Handle sensitive data safely**
* Make pragmatic tradeoffs between speed and compliance
* Design secure systems without over-engineering

**Success Criteria**

You’ll know you’re succeeding when:

* Work is delivered with clarity, minimal rework, and aligned to business priorities
* The new platform is being built cleanly and efficiently
* The existing system becomes more stable and easier to work with
* Architecture becomes simpler over time
* Engineering workflows, standards, and testing are clearly defined and adopted
* The team ships faster with fewer regressions

**Why Join**

* High ownership and high impact as you shape both the system and the team
* Ability to closely work with business stakeholders and impact the direction of development
* Work on real-world complexity across healthcare, ecommerce, and AI
* Direct influence on architecture, standards, and product direction
* A team that values speed, pragmatism, and getting things done

Pay: $130,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

* Do you have healthcare experience?
* If so, how many years of healthcare experience do you have?
* Do you use AI coding tools in your regular development work?
* In the past 6 months, roughly how many times have you rejected or significantly rewritten AI-generated code because it was incorrect, insecure, or poorly designed?
* Do you have technical skills in the following core stacks: Python, C#m and NextJS?
* Do you have hands-on experience building, integrating, and maintaining a live e-commerce platform (e.g., product catalogs, orders, subscriptions, or payments)?
* How many years of hands-on experience do you have developing and maintaining a production e-commerce platform?

About GitHub: GitHub is the world’s leading platform for agentic software development — powered by Copilot to build, scale, and deliver secure software. Over 180 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, and more than 77,000 organisations have adopted GitHub Copilot.  
Locations: In this role you can work from Remote, United States  
Overview:

GitHub is shaping the future of software development in the age of AI agents — and search is at the heart of it. As GitHub's lexical and semantic code search engine, Blackbird powers context retrieval for business-critical experiences across the platform and our Copilot products, including Cloud Agent, Code Review, Copilot CLI, and VS Code.

We're looking for a **Senior Software Engineer** to help develop, scale, operate and extend Blackbird. This role is specifically focused on infrastructure, operations, automation, CI/CD, DX, observability, and security. You'll be part of our Copilot Agents organization, positively impacting millions of software developers and AI agents around the world who are building everything from open source to global enterprises.

We are looking for creative problem solvers and diverse thinkers, people who care about culture as well as customers and features. We believe that how we do things is as important as what we do. Big vision, a common purpose, passion for quality, curiosity, dedication, and investment in fun and collaboration are what lead to great results. Great products reflect the teams that build them.

More of the world’s development data lives on GitHub than anywhere else. Helping developers navigate and understand that data is a core part of GitHub’s mission, and an area with significant potential we have only begun to realize. We have high aspirations for how we can help developers understand and navigate code, and for making collaboration more seamless. The foundation for these efforts is our purpose-built code search engine which powers lexical and semantic code search in GitHub’s core search experience as well as GitHub’s Copilot products.

The ideal candidate has strong experience with distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, reliability engineering, as well as the ability to work autonomously, learn quickly, and communicate and set technical direction. You will be working within a strong team of staff and principal engineers as well as collaborate with partner teams across the Copilot Agents organization.

As a software engineer at GitHub, you will enhance the collaboration experience at GitHub by working closely with a community of engineers and designers with a distributed, diverse and passionate team delivering the services that millions of developers depend on. In this role you will design, prototype, implement, ship and support highly performant and globally scalable code search technology with your team.

Responsibilities:

* Own and advocate for the health and quality of the systems that the team builds, including participating in on-call and first responder rotations.
* Drives efforts to collect, classify, and analyze data on a range of metrics (e.g., health of the system, where bugs might be occurring).
* Drives the refinement of products through data analytics, and makes informed decisions in engineering products through data integration.
* Considers and drives comprehensive application of automation within production and deployment of a product.
* Runs code in simulated or other non-production environments to confirm functionality and error-free runtime for products.
* Improves development quality, development velocity, and team performance through modeling contributions to improvement of developer tooling.
* Drives efforts to ensure the correct processes are followed to achieve a high degree of security, privacy, safety, and accessibility.
* Creates and ensures the presence of visible evidence (e.g., audit logs, system reports, security compliance) to demonstrate compliance for products.
* Leverages subject-matter expertise of product features, incorporates service health indicators (e.g., SLOs) to prioritize work focused on, and partners with appropriate stakeholders (e.g., project managers) to drive collaboration on the workgroup's project plans, release plans, and work items.
* Write architecture briefs and proposals, carry out code experiments, and build prototypes to learn how we can achieve planetary scale with our systems.
* Design and implement APIs to facilitate seamless integration between software components.
* Utilize CI/CD tools to set up automated pipelines for continuous integration and delivery.
* Become intimately familiar with the systems you build and take pride in writing maintainable code.
* Design, develop, test and ship high-quality technical solutions that scale across multiple GitHub services.

Qualifications:

**Required Qualifications:**

* 6+ years experience in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline with proven experience maintaining and delivering production software coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, or Python
  + OR Associate’s Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 5+ years experience in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline with proven experience maintaining and delivering production software coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, or Python
  + OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 4+ years experience in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline with proven experience maintaining and delivering production software coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, or Python
  + OR Master's Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field AND 2+ years experience in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical discipline with proven experience maintaining and delivering production software coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, or Python
  + OR Doctorate in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Math, Physics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field
  + OR equivalent experience.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Understanding of production system monitoring and observability with skills across network, application, caching, queuing, load-balancing, storage and distributed services layers.
* Passionate about fostering good engineering practices and processes with solid understanding of testing principles and high-quality software.
* 2+ years experience in systems programming, search index internals and information retrieval.
* Prior experience solving problems with large-scale, distributed systems is preferred.

**About Rippling**
------------------

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Take onboarding, for example. With Rippling, you can hire a new employee anywhere in the world and set up their payroll, corporate card, computer, benefits, and even third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365—all within 90 seconds.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

**About the IT Product Team**
-----------------------------

The IT Product Engineering team is critical to unifying Rippling's workforce management system, bridging the gap between HR and traditional IT administration. Our mission is to build software that enables businesses to manage employee devices, applications, and access security automatically, leveraging Rippling's single source of employee truth (the HRIS). We automate the complexity of IT management from the moment a new employee is hired to the moment they offboard.

### **What We Build**

We build the mission-critical software that simplifies IT for organizations, turning complex, manual processes into simple, one-click solutions. Our core product domains include:

* **Device Management (MDM):** Developing systems to securely enroll, configure, manage, and inventory corporate devices (macOS, Windows, iOS, etc.), including policy enforcement and remote wipe capabilities.
* **App Management & Identity:** Creating the centralized platform for provisioning and de-provisioning employee access to hundreds of third-party SaaS applications, ensuring instant security and compliance through integrated identity and access management (IAM).
* **Inventory & Asset Management:** Building the core financial and logistical systems to track physical assets, manage software licenses, and automate IT procurement from device ordering to deployment.
* **Security & Compliance:** Developing the mechanisms for setting, managing, and enforcing security policies across all devices and applications, ensuring employee and corporate data remain protected.

**What you will do**
--------------------

* Design, implement, and test reliable backend services and APIs that power core product features and business logic at scale.
* Work across key technical domains, including API design, data modeling, event modeling, and optimizing service performance.
* Own the development lifecycle for defined features, from implementation and testing to deployment, monitoring, and support in a production environment.
* Effectively integrate into cross-functional teams, contribute to technical discovery, and rapidly learn from code and system feedback.

**What you will need**
----------------------

* 2+ years of professional experience as a backend engineer, preferably with Python, Go, or a similar production language, and strong experience with relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL).
* Care about business impact, balancing technical craft with speed and the bottom line to deliver value quickly.
* Ability to thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments, demonstrating resilience and agility in the face of changing product needs.
* Excellent skills in communicating complex technical ideas with clarity to enable effective collaboration with peers and stakeholders.

Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform.

**The Role**
------------

An auction closes and every seller in it gets paid in the same moment, each against a different fee schedule — some by ACH, some by wire, some instant. A buyer funds a five-figure purchase and the bank returns it three days later. A webhook arrives twice, out of order, from a provider that was down for an hour. Every one of those movements has to reach the right account, on the right rail, at the right time, and land in the ledger exactly once.

That is the whole job. You own how money physically moves at Alt: the providers, the rails, the orchestration layer that routes between them, and the risk posture that keeps a marketplace of high-value transactions safe. The ledger team owns the record; you own everything that happens between a customer's bank and that record. You are not building a checkout flow. You are building the liquidity that makes this marketplace work.

The KPI: 99.99% reliability on gateway and banking integrations, and a time-to-funds for sellers and borrowers that we measure, publish, and beat every quarter. In payments, "mostly working" is a failure.

The people who are great at this have integrated a provider that lied to them, and they design for the third retry, the late return, and the duplicate callback because they've been on the wrong side of all three.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

**Rails and money movement.** ACH origination and returns, RTP and other instant rails, wires, cards, and stablecoin settlement. A $300K wire and a $300 ACH debit are different products with different controls, and you'll design for both. Credit-push rails change what you can auto-charge and when funds are final — you'll own those product consequences, not just the integration.

**Provider architecture and orchestration.** Multi-PSP integrations built so the next one isn't a rewrite, and a single orchestration layer that routes each movement to the right provider by cost, speed, and health. Webhooks, idempotency, retry semantics, state machines, failure modes on the third retry, and provider failover that nobody notices.

**Payouts and collections.** Getting sellers and borrowers their money faster than anyone else in this market: instant payout options, batch payouts at auction close, and the rail and timing choices that make them safe. On the other side, cash advance disbursement and the scheduled auto-pay batches that collect repayments run on your rails. The ledger team decides what a pending balance means; you decide how and when the money actually moves.

**Risk on high-value flows.** The fraud, dispute, and chargeback posture for a marketplace where one bad transaction is a five- or six-figure problem. Holds, limits, and settlement windows set with data — and you'll know what each one costs in conversion. Step-up verification triggered by risk signals rather than blanket friction.

**Payment operations.** When a transfer is stuck, a return code is unfamiliar, or a provider goes quiet mid-batch, you find out why. You'll own the tooling that lets operations and support answer "where is my money" without paging an engineer, and you'll feed clean, complete processor data to the ledger team's reconciliation so their breaks are real breaks and not missing webhooks.

**The posting contract, from the producer side.** Every movement you originate lands in the ledger through a typed contract the ledger team owns. You'll build against it, push on it when a new rail doesn't fit, and guarantee exactly-once delivery into it.

**The trade-off calls.** Shipping speed against uncompromising reliability; build custom versus buy an orchestration platform. You'll be asked to defend both directions.

**The team.** Be a multiplier through rigorous code reviews, technical documentation, and mentorship.

**How You'll Use AI Here**
--------------------------

We don't want to hear that you use Claude every day. Everyone does. We want to know what you've built with it. Concretely, in this role:

* Turn a payment provider or bank partner integration spec into a typed client and a test suite in an afternoon instead of a sprint — including the ACH return codes and reversal paths nobody wants to hand-write
* Stand up a rail simulator that produces the failures a sandbox won't: a late return, a duplicate callback, a partial reversal, a webhook that arrives twice out of order, a settlement that lands after the window closed. Then run the orchestration layer against it
* Build an agent that watches provider health, webhook lag, and return rates, and proposes a routing change or a hold before the on-call sees the alert
* Put an MCP server over provider APIs and our payment state so "why did this payout fail" is a question support asks in plain language
* Use models to generate adversarial test cases for the orchestration state machine — the provider that acks and then times out, the failover mid-batch, the return that hits after the payout cleared — and find the transitions nobody specified
* Use Claude Code or Cursor as the default way you work through a provider migration or a refactor, not as autocomplete

If you've built agents, wired up connectors, written skills or MCP servers, or shipped internal tooling your team actually depends on — lead with that. Name the artifact, not the tool.

**What You Bring**
------------------

* 5+ years of experience with a heavy focus on backend systems — Python, Postgres, AWS.
* You've worked on real money movement. ACH origination and returns, RTP or FedNow, wires, or equivalent. You know what an R01 is, why NACHA return windows matter, and why a credit-push rail changes the product flow and not just the API call.
* You've integrated more than one payment provider in production, and you've lived through one of them failing.
* You've handled large transactions, where the failure mode is a five- or six-figure problem and someone notices immediately.
* You're API-native. Webhooks, idempotency, eventual consistency, and exactly-once delivery are your default vocabulary.
* Strong SQL and relational design. You know how to write a transaction that won't fail under load — including at auction close and during scheduled auto-pay batches.
* Marketplace or two-sided flow experience. Buyers and sellers, settlement between them, and the timing tension that creates.
* An obsession with reliability. You think deeply about idempotency, race conditions, and what happens on the third retry.
* Product-owner thinking. You don't just build a pay button. You understand the flow of funds and how to communicate financial status clearly to a user who is worried about their money.
* Pragmatism. You know when to build a custom internal solution and when to leverage a third party to get the job done.

**Strongly preferred:** direct experience with Stripe, Plaid, Airwallex, PayPal, Modern Treasury, or Increase, and with evaluating or building a payment orchestration layer across more than one of them.

**Strong plus:** fraud, dispute, or chargeback work on a marketplace; hands-on with risk tooling like Sardine, Sift, or Stripe Radar; enough React and TypeScript to ship the payment-method and payout surfaces you own.

**Bonus:** distributed systems; stablecoin or on-chain settlement; KYC/KYB, bank partnership, or bank-sponsor program exposure; the alternative asset space. You collect, or you have a view on where this market is going.

**How We'll Interview You**
---------------------------

We'll be specific so you can prepare. Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, and try selling — go through the workflows. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go. For this role, look specifically at the deposit, payment method, and payout surfaces.

* **Recruiter screen** — 25 minutes, Google Meet. Come ready to talk about the metric you own today and how you're performing against it, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We'll answer your questions.
* **Hiring manager** — 45 minutes, Google Meet. Be ready to go deep on the provider integration or money-movement system closest to your own hands: what you built versus inherited, the trade-offs you made, and what you'd change now.
* **Technical screen** — 60 minutes. A hands-on working session on a rail behaving badly — duplicate and out-of-order webhooks, a late return, a provider that acks and then times out — and a payout batch that has to complete exactly once. Think out loud.
* **Architecture and system design** — 60 minutes. Design a payment orchestration layer under real constraints: two providers, failover mid-batch, instant and batch payouts, a risk hold on a five-figure transfer, and a ledger contract you don't control. We'll push back on at least one of your choices on purpose — how you take that matters as much as the design.
* **Culture interview** — 30 minutes. How you work with the people who depend on your systems — operations, finance, support, and the customer on the other end of a held transfer.
* **Leore, our founder and CEO** — 30 minutes. Everyone who joins Alt meets Leore. Come with a point of view on where you'd take Alt's money movement first.
* **Reference check(s)** — 15 minutes with a former manager(s).

This is a full-time, fully remote Software Engineer role with an annual salary of $100,000 USD.

A closer look at the work

This role connects the product people see with the services that make it work. A feature may start with an applicant uploading a résumé, continue through a background worker preparing application materials, and finish with a status update or an email. You will help make those transitions reliable and understandable. The employer side has a similar journey: a hiring team creates a role, publishes it, receives candidate applications, and follows up through the hiring pipeline.

Product and interface development

Build interfaces that make the next action clear. Improve form validation, loading states, error messages, accessibility, and responsive layouts. Help users understand what has been saved, what is in progress, and what needs their input. Work on application review screens, profile editing, résumé previews, and employer workflows. Keep important actions usable when services are slow or a third-party integration is unavailable.

Backend systems and integrations

Develop APIs and background workflows that can recover from failures. Keep task state durable, avoid duplicate actions, and record evidence when an external system confirms an outcome. Integrate email events, payments, job data, and employer forms using the appropriate API or browser workflow. Treat timeouts, retries, changing form fields, and partial responses as normal engineering problems that need clear behavior and useful diagnostics.

Automation and AI features

Help improve the preparation of résumé edits, cover letters, and application answers. Use structured outputs and validation so generated material remains grounded in information the user provided. Build tests around the difficult cases, including missing information and mismatched inputs. Hiring tools

Improve the Careers site, application intake, résumé storage, screening questions, written interviews, and candidate communications. Candidate assessment should support the hiring team; people remain responsible for hiring decisions.

Start by understanding the user’s problem and the existing workflow. Break the work into changes that can be reviewed and tested. Explain important tradeoffs, document integrations where needed, and investigate the cause of a failure rather than only its symptom. Pay attention to sensitive data, authentication boundaries, and what information is passed to outside services. Prefer useful tests that exercise meaningful behavior over checks that simply repeat the implementation.

* Reduce the time it takes to load an applicant’s workspace without loading unrelated data first.

* Make an application workflow recover cleanly after an email verification or an employer form change.

* Improve a résumé review experience so users can see, accept, and confirm each change.

* Build an applicant intake flow that reliably saves a résumé and sends the next-step email.

* Add monitoring that makes stalled tasks, provider errors, and unexpected duplicate actions easy to investigate.

**About Handshake AI**

Human data is the core infrastructure to AI advancement. Frontier AI labs currently improve model capabilities with various data-intensive post-training techniques. We believe that data spend for AI training will increase by 3-5x in the next few years and continue for much longer as models take on new domains. Handshake AI supports all of the frontier AI labs, working on their most complex data at the largest scale.

**The Role**
============

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to make development at Handshake faster, more reliable, and easier to understand.

Coding agents are a core part of how our engineers work. Both need reliable tools, useful instructions, and clear feedback to produce code we can trust. You’ll build and improve tools that run builds and tests, review changes, and explain failures. Your work will help engineers and agents spend less time waiting or debugging and more time building.

You’ll care as much about how a tool feels to use as whether it works. Is it fast? Are the next steps clear? Does an error message help someone solve the problem? You’ll use developer surveys, conversations with engineers, and system data to guide improvements.

You don’t need a background in developer tools or AI. We’re looking for strong coding skills, curiosity, and a desire to make complex systems easier to use.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build and maintain tools for builds, tests, code review, and merging changes. Make them useful for both engineers and coding agents.
* Find and fix slow builds, unreliable tests, and confusing errors. Address the cause rather than asking users to work around the problem.
* Make tests faster and more reliable. Split work across machines, reuse previous results when safe, and keep tests from interfering with one another.
* Make failures easier to understand. Help users see what went wrong and what they can do next.
* Improve the tools, instructions, and environments that coding agents use to write, test, and debug code.
* Help build automated code reviews and checks. Reduce repetitive work while keeping clear standards for quality and safety.
* Use developer surveys and direct feedback to find problems worth solving. Work with teammates to release improvements safely, then check whether they made a difference.
* Share what you learn through documentation, code reviews, and working sessions with other engineers.

**You Have**
------------

* About 3–5 years of professional software engineering experience, or comparable hands-on experience.
* Strong JavaScript or TypeScript skills and experience in the JavaScript ecosystem. Your background may be server-side, such as Node.js or Bun, or browser-based.
* Hands-on experience with JavaScript unit testing and end to end tests with tools like Jest, Vitest and Playwright.
* Experience shipping and maintaining production software, including writing automated tests.
* A careful approach to debugging. You test your assumptions and follow the evidence to find the cause.
* Curiosity about unfamiliar code and the patience to learn how a system works.
* A high bar for user experience. You notice small frustrations, listen to users, and care about the details that make tools easy to use.
* The ability to finish clearly defined projects on your own. You also know when to ask for help or work through a problem with a teammate.
* Clear communication and a willingness to give feedback, learn from others, and share what you know.

**Extra Credit**
----------------

You don’t need to know every tool we use. Any of the following would be helpful:

* Work on build systems or continuous integration (CI), using tools such as Buildkite, GitHub Actions, Docker, or Kubernetes.
* Experience building or extending test frameworks and shared libraries that make authoring tests more efficient and reliable.
* Experience making tests faster or fixing tests that fail without a code change.
* Hands-on use of coding agents, including giving them useful instructions and checking their results.
* Work on automated code review or testing, with or without AI.
* Experience making software builds and releases reliable and secure.
* Use of logs, metrics, or traces to investigate problems.

Explore our mission, values, and comprehensive US benefits at joinhandshake.com/careers.
